findings.reason: the plan must name the source (the run record's `node.id`, read through the run's pointer) or pass the reviewed node id in, or the node will be built around the wrong identifier and the very case written for it cannot be written as stated.
findings.text: §27's deliverable names `<n>` as "the reviewed run's node id", but the function it modifies takes no node id, and the only identifier the caller has is a different one: `compose_repair_for_run` binds `node_id = str(composed["node_id"])` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1115`), which `compose_repair_for_run` in `reckon/crew/repair.py` fills from `repair_node_id(...)` — a `repair-<source>-<head>` round id, not the reviewed run's node id; an implementer taking the available value grants `tests/test_repair_a_merge_refuses_…_<sha>.py` while the plan's case 1 expects `tests/test_<reviewed node>.py`, so the plan does not say where the path's name comes from

findings.reason: without a case asserting the advice names the test path, the plan's own goal (a worker that does not block asking for a scope it cannot see) is not measured by its gate.
findings.text: the three cases assert the grant only, but what the resumed worker reads is the advice line: `_grant_round_scope` returns `advised = [path for path in scope if path not in refused]` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:496`) built from its *input* scope, and `_repair_resume_advice` prints exactly that list after `Write scope for this round:` (line 550), so a test path granted beyond the composed scope never reaches the worker, while the coordinator's own repair in the cited incident did name it ("tests/test_merge_requires_promotable_run.py is now in your write scope", `resume-2-advice.txt`); an implementation that widens the claim and returns `advised` unchanged passes every stated case

findings.reason: the grant's reason is the audit trail for an out-of-scope write, and a case with two blocking findings (the second asking for the test) is what tells the implementer to pass the asking finding's id rather than reuse `_grant_reason`.
findings.text: case 1 requires the granted test path to carry "the finding id as its reason", but the existing reason reader matches on the finding's `file`: `_grant_reason` returns the id of the finding whose `file` equals or prefixes the path and otherwise falls back to `findings[0]["id"]` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:500–516`), and no finding names `tests/test_<n>.py`, so a round with more than one blocking finding records the first finding's id; the done-when case uses a single finding, where the fallback happens to be the right one

response_events.note: §27: <n> comes from the reviewed run's pointer node id; the test path is added to the advised write scope the resumed worker reads; its grant reason is the asking finding's id, set explicitly; cases cover two blocking findings and the advice line
